fact: The breast of the Swan — a luminous supergiant at the heart of the Northern Cross, wrapped in glowing gas.
bio: Sadr (Gamma Cygni) is a yellow-white supergiant roughly 1,800 light-years away, sitting at the intersection of the Northern Cross where the wings of Cygnus meet the body. It is embedded against a vast complex of glowing hydrogen known as the Sadr region.
cultural: The name is Arabic for 'the chest' or 'breast'. As the centre of the Northern Cross, Sadr rides the brightest reach of the summer Milky Way, in the direction of one of its richest star clouds.
